title: Installing Hot Chocolate
description: Set up a .NET Core project and add the Hot Chocolate GraphQL server.

data.text: Hot Chocolate is distributed as NuGet packages. You can add it to a new or existing ASP.NET Core project.

data.code:
dotnet new webapi -n GraphQLDemo
dotnet new classlib -n GraphQLDemo.Types

data.text: Add the Hot Chocolate server and the Hot Chocolate ASP.NET Core integration:

data.code:
dotnet add package HotChocolate.AspNetCore
# Optional: for diagnostics
# dotnet add package HotChocolate.Diagnostics

data.text: Register the GraphQL server in `Program.cs` using the minimal API style introduced in .NET 6.

data.title: IDE Support
data.text: Visual Studio, Rider, and VS Code all provide excellent Hot Chocolate support, including schema validation and autocompletion.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hot Chocolate is installed via NuGet
data.takeaway: We'll define our first query and type in the next lesson.
